478: \section{Computational Setup and Signal Modeling}\label{sec:setup}
479: \subsection{Model Implementation}
480: We implement the SM Lagrangian with Goldstone boson couplings in the Feynman gauge 
481: and the Lagrangian terms of Eqs.~(\ref{chcurrent})-(\ref{neucurrent}) in the Unitary gauge
482: into FR 2.3.10~\cite{Alloul:2013bka,Christensen:2008py}.
483: $R_2$ rational and QCD renormalization counter terms are calculated with~\nloct~1.02~\cite{Degrande:2014vpa} and FeynArts 3.8~\cite{Hahn:2000kx}.
484: UFO model files are publicly available from the FR model database~\cite{nloFRModel}, 
485: and can be ported into modern event generators, including
486: \mgamc~\cite{Alwall:2014hca},
487: HERWIG~\cite{Bellm:2015jjp}, and SHERPA~\cite{Gleisberg:2008ta}.
488: 
489: \subsection{Monte Carlo Configuration}
490: Fully differential results at LO and NLO are obtained using \mgamc~\confirm{2.5.$\beta$2}~\cite{Alwall:2014hca}.
491: Events are parton showered and hadronized using Pythia~\confirm{8.219} (PY8)~\cite{Sjostrand:2014zea},
492: and passed to MadAnalysis5~\confirm{v1.4}~\cite{Conte:2012fm} for particle-level clustering.
493: Unless stated otherwise, jets are clustered via FastJet~\confirm{3.2.1}~\cite{Cacciari:2005hq,Cacciari:2011ma} 
494: according to the anti-$k_T$ algorithm~\cite{Cacciari:2008gp} with a separation scale of $R = 0.4$.
495: 
496: LRSM inputs are given in Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmInputs}). SM inputs are taken from the 2014 Particle Data Group~\cite{Agashe:2014kda}:
497: \begin{eqnarray}
498:  \alpha^{\rm \overline{MS}}(M_{Z}) = 1/127.940, \quad 
499:  M_{Z} = 91.1876\GeV, \quad
500:  \sin^{2}_{\rm \overline{MS}}(\theta_{W}) = 0.23126.
501:  \label{eq:smInputs}
502: \end{eqnarray}
503: We use the NLO NNPDF3.0 parton distribution function (PDF) set~(\texttt{lhaid=260000})~\cite{Ball:2014uwa} for LO and NLO calculations.
504: PDFs and $\as(\mu_r)$ are extracted using LHAPDF 6.1.6~\cite{Buckley:2014ana}.
505: 
506: For all processes, we equate the renormalization $(\mu_r)$ and factorization $(\mu_f)$ scales.
507: We choose as a dynamical scale, half the sum over all final-state transverse energies:
508: \begin{equation}
509:  \mu_r, \mu_f = \mu_0 \equiv \sum_{k=N,\ell,\text{jets}}\cfrac{E_{T,k}}{2} = \frac12\sum_{k} \sqrt{m_k^2 + p_{T,k}^2}
510:  \label{eq:mgScale}
511: \end{equation}
512: At NLO, we estimate the residual uncertainty from missing higher order terms by simultaneously varying $\mu_{r},\mu_f$ over the range:
513: \begin{equation}
514:  0.5\times\mu_0 ~<~ \mu_{r},\mu_f ~<~ 2\times\mu_0.
515: \end{equation}
516: 
517: 
518: Instructions for using the Effective LRSM at NLO within the \mgamc~framework are provided in App.~\ref{app:sigDef}.
519: 
520: For total inclusive cross sections reported in Sec.~\ref{sec:ppXSec} and \ref{sec:epXSec}, no phase space cuts are applied.
521: 
522: To study the properties of $N$ jets and $t$ jets, we consider the processes 
523: \begin{equation}
524:  p ~p ~\rightarrow \WR^{\pm (*)} ~\rightarrow Ne^\pm, ~tb, ~\text{and}~q\overline{q'}, \quad\text{for}\quad q\in\{u,d,c,s\}, 
525:  \label{eq:lhcNLOPSprocesses}
526: \end{equation}
527: at NLO in QCD. We include hard QCD radiation off the final-state quarks and a finite $\WR$ width.
528: While we neglect interference with the SM $W$ for simplicity, it is possible to implement it within our framework.
529: To minimize the contamination of far off-shell $\WR$ with virtualities $Q^2\ll \MWR^{2}$,
530: we impose a generator-level cut on $X\in\{N,t,q\}$ and require $p_T^X > 750\GeV$.
531: While the cut on light quarks is trivial in \mgamc
532: restrictions on on-shell heavy neutrinos and top quarks require implementing a user-defined cut into the phase space integration routine.
533: This can be done in a straightforward manner; see App.~\ref{app:GenCuts} for instructions.
534: 
535: \subsection{Spin-Correlated Decays of $N$ and $t$ with Improved MadSpin}
536: We decay $N$ and $t$ via MadSpin~\cite{Artoisenet:2012st}, thus retaining full spin correlation, just before parton showering.
537: However, three body decays like $N\rightarrow \ell^\pm\WR^{\mp*}\rightarrow\ell^\pm q\overline{q'}$ are not supported in current releases of MadSpin.

\section{EffLRSM@NLO Signal Simulation with \mgamc}\label{app:sigDef}
In this section, we provide brief instructions for simulating particle production in the Effective LRSM using the MG5\_aMC@NLO+PY8 framework
for FO and PS predictions.

The inclusive $pp\rightarrow\WR$ cross section at NLO can be calculated for $\MWR\in[1\TeV,6\TeV]$ in 1 TeV increments
with the scale choice of Eq.~(\ref{eq:mgScale}) via the \mgamc~commands:
\begin{verbatim}
> import model EffLRSM_NLO
> define p  = u c d s b u~ c~ d~ s~ b~ g
> define j  = p
> define wr = wr+ wr-
> generate p p > wr [QCD]
> output PP_WR_NLO; launch
> order=NLO 
> fixed_order=ON
> set MWR scan:range(1000,6001,1000)
> set dynamical_scale_choice 3
\end{verbatim}
In the same environment, the LO cross section at, say, 100 TeV can be computed with the following:
\begin{verbatim}
> launch PP_WR_NLO
> order=LO
> set LHC 100
\end{verbatim}
Inclusive $pp\rightarrow\ZR$ production rates are obtained by making the obvious \texttt{wr}$~\rightarrow~$\texttt{zr} substitution.

To simulate $pp\rightarrow \WR \rightarrow Ne^\pm$ at NLO+PS with finite $\WR$ width effects, the commands are:
\begin{verbatim}
> generate p p > wr+ > n1 e+ [QCD]

> output PP_WR_Ne_NLO; launch
\end{verbatim}
Other leptons, e.g., $N_2$ or $\tau^\pm$, can appear in the final state but may require regeneration of the LRSM UFO;
default lepton mixing is set according to Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmNuMixing}).
For $\WR^*\rightarrow tb$, the commands are:
\begin{verbatim}
> generate p p > wr+ > t b~ [QCD]
> add process p p > wr- > t~ b [QCD]
> output PP_WR_tb_NLO; launch
\end{verbatim}

Simulating inclusive $e^-p\rightarrow N+X$ production at LO for $\MWR=3\TeV$ and $\mN\in[100\GeV,1\TeV]$ in 100 GeV increments 
can be done using the following:
\begin{verbatim}
> generate generate e- p > n1 j
> output PP_ep_NX_LO; launch
> set lpp1 0
> set ebeam1 140
> set ebeam2 7000
> set polbeam1 80
> set MWR 3000
> set mn1 scan:range(100,1001,100)
\end{verbatim}
The third line turns off the PDF for the electron beam, whereas the fourth and fifth line sets the individual beam energies.
The line after sets the electron beam polarization to $P_e = +80\%$.

\section{Three-Body Decays of $N$ and $t$ in MadSpin}\label{app:MadSpin}
As shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:Decay}, decays of the lightest heavy neutrino in the LRSM 
are dominated by the process $N\rightarrow \ell^\pm W^{\mp *}_R \rightarrow \ell^\pm q \overline{q'}$. 
Here $\WR$ is far off-shell.
To model such processes using MadSpin within the \mgamc framework requires adding to \texttt{Cards/madspin\_card.dat} the following:
\begin{verbatim}
set spinmode onshell 
define  q = u c d s u~ c~ d~ s~ 
define ee = e+ e- 
decay  n1 > ee q q
launch
\end{verbatim}
For top quarks decaying to hadronic and leptonic final states, we use the following MadSpin syntax:
\begin{verbatim}
decay t  > w+ b,  w+ > all all
decay t~ > w- b~, w- > all all
launch
\end{verbatim}
In both cases, we retain full spin correlation with the hard process matrix elements.

## Objective
- Extract the complete new-physics content of the EffLRSM model (arXiv:1610.08985) from its LaTeX source into a `spec.json` FeynRulesModel object, run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate until valid.
- Final deliverable: a message containing the self-audit tab (format per TASK.md); `spec.json` written in the current directory.

## Important Details
- Working directory: `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-EffLRSM-5kxupzbf/` (stay inside it). Bash DENIED except `./frgen *`; use `glob`/`read`/`write` tools. Reads truncate at 2000 chars/line and by line limit — read in chunks.
- Model name must be `"EffLRSM_gen"`; JSON only in `spec.json`.
- Schema rules: all numeric physics values STRINGS (`"-1/3"`, `"1500."`, `"1.*^12"`); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups: []`; standard indices (Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W) need no declaration; other indices need `index_decls` (`range_kind "NoUnfold"`, correct size); unique `class_index` per particle; `self_conjugate=false` for complex, `true` for real/Majorana; no charges on self-conjugate fields; unique class names; `InteractionOrder {NP,1}` on new coupling params (hierarchy must include NP — declare `{{"QCD",1},{"QED",2},{"NP",1}}` to preserve SM orders when add-on file overwrites `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy`); completeness is scored.
- `TASK.md` is 91 lines, fully read (task, schema rules, output instructions, TOOLKIT/self-audit tab section in tail).
- Paper structure mapped by grep: theory §2 lines 274–430, constraints 431, limits 454, setup 478–535, results 560+, appendix 1017+; lines 498–1736 verified to contain only MC setup/results/references/appendix instructions — no additional model particles/parameters.

### Model content extracted from paper (verified)
- New particles: `WR` complex vector (QuantumNumbers `{Q->1, Y->1}`; mass `"3000."`, width `"84.3"`); `ZR` real self-conjugate vector (mass `"5070."`, width `"114."`, no QuantumNumbers); Majorana class `NR` members `N1,N2,N3` (self-conjugate, masses `"173.3"`, `"1.*^12"`, `"1.*^12"`; WN1 = `"2.12*^-8"`, wn2/wn3 placeholder `"1."`). `N` is protected ⇒ never a bare class name. New width params avoid SM's `WW`/`WZ` ⇒ `WWR`, `WZR`.
- Mass symbol naming: paper's MG commands use `set MWR` and `set mn1` ⇒ prefer mass syms `MWR`, `MZR`, `mn1/mn2/mn3` (matching the real model file).
- No mixing in this effective model (aligned mass eigenstates); benchmark X_{ℓm}=0 ⇒ drop `\overline{ν^c}X` term (avoid `CC[...]` risk).
- Verified equations: quark current `-κ_R^q g/√2 Σ ū_i V^{CKM'}_ij W_R^+ γ^μ P_R d_j + H.c.`; lepton current `-κ_R^ℓ g/√2 Σ_ℓ [Σ_{m'} \overline{N_{m'}} Y_{ℓm'}] W_R^+ γ^μ P_R ℓ^- + H.c.`; ZR prefactor `-κ_R^f g/Sqrt[1-(1/κ_R^f)^2 tan²θW]`, `g_L=(T3L−Q)tan²θW/κ²`, `g_R=T3R−tan²θW·Q/κ²`.
- Chirality algebra: `N̄ γ^μ P_R ℓ = N̄_R γ^μ ℓ_R`; render as `NRbar.yN.Ga[mu].ProjP.l`. Rule 13 matrix idiom: `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`. No HC on neutral ZR terms.
- g_L identical for both SU(2)L doublet members (u_L/d_L: −(1/6)t/κ²; ν_L/e_L: +(1/2)t/κ²) ⇒ explicit component terms chosen (physical fields `uq,dq,l,vl` avoid the CKM dressing that `QL`'s Definitions would inject).
- Derived chiral coefficients (t = tan²θW): `gZLq = -(1/6) t/kappaRq^2`; `gZRu = 1/2-(2/3) t/kappaRq^2`; `gZRd = -1/2+(1/3) t/kappaRq^2`; `gZLl = (1/2) t/kappaRl^2`; `gZRe = -1/2 + t/kappaRl^2`; `gZRN = 1/2`; ZR prefactors written inline (`-kappaRq gw/Sqrt[1-tan2thetaW/kappaRq^2]`, leptons with `kappaRl`).
- Width cross-checks (Γ = N_c κ² g² M/(48π)·phase), MS inputs t=0.30083, g²≈0.4246: e+e− 3×2.533=7.60 ✓(7.64), ν 3×0.921=2.76 ✓(2.78), N1N1 10.17 ✓(10.2), tt 11.27 ✓(11.3), ZR total 114 ✓ internally consistent; quarks 78.2 vs 82.3 (with on-shell sw2: t=0.287, g²=0.4405 → 83.0 ✓). Decision: `tan2thetaW = sw2/(1-sw2)` using SM.sw2.
- WR widths: per massless pair 25.32 (=50.7/2 pairs ✓), tb 25.19 ✓(25.2), ℓN per flavor 8.39 ✓(8.41, |Y|=1). **Corrected inconsistency**: table Total 84.3 = 50.7+25.2+8.41 omits 2 of the 3 lepton channels (sum formula ⇒ 101.1). Use 84.3 (paper's table), note discrepancy in self-audit.
- Hypercharge relation (LRSM): `Y = T3R + (B−L)/2` — verified against SM chiral fields (Y(u_L)=1/6, u_R=2/3, ℓ_L=−1/2, e_R=−1); ⇒ Y(WR+)=1, Y(ZR)=Y(N)=0. Declare `{Q->1, Y->1}` on WR only (self-conjugate ZR/NR take no charges). Y sums per term = 0; Q sums = 0; B−L sums = 0 with B−L(q)=1/3, B−L(ℓ)=−1, B−L(N)=−1, WR/ZR=0; B−L not declared anywhere in model (state in audit) — re-derivation not needed (no new-U(1)-charged scalars; no new Yukawas).
- Parameter plan: `kappaRq`, `kappaRl` (External, `"1."`, `{NP,1}`, order_block 1/2, block `LRSM`); `yN` 3×3 External tensor, identity via 9 explicit value_rules (yN[m',ℓ] = Y_{ℓm'} transpose), own LHA block; `VCKMR` 3×3 External tensor identity, **distinct LHA block** (entry-collision rule); Internal `tan2thetaW` = `sw2/(1-sw2)` (no order, mirrors orderless SM `sw2`); Internal `gZLq,gZRu,gZRd,gZLl,gZRe,gZRN` with `{NP,1}`; topo sort handles dependencies.
- Lagrangian terms planned: `LWRkin` (`-1/2 FS[WRbar,mu,nu] FS[WR,mu,nu] + MWR^2 WRbar[mu] WR[mu]`), `LZRkin` (`-1/4 FS[ZR,mu,nu] FS[ZR,mu,nu] + 1/2 MZR^2 ZR[mu] ZR[mu]`), `LNkin` (`I/2 NRbar.Ga[mu].del[NR,mu]` + member-wise Majorana masses), `LWRqq` (+HC), `LWRlnu` (+HC), `LZRq`, `LZRl`, `LZRv` (light ν), `LZRn` (heavy N), `LTotal` = sum of all. Names containing `kin` are skipped by lint's missing_interaction_order rule.
- Majorana mass-term risk analyzed: `NRbar.N1` may leave Generation index uncontracted ⇒ prefer member bars `-1/2 mn1 N1bar.N1 - 1/2 mn2 N2bar.N2 - 1/2 mn3 N3bar.N3` (member symbols get auto anti-fields; class-level sym `Mn` unused, avoids lint `majorana_mass_no_half` which needs literal class sym). Fallback: three separate N classes.
- Lint specifics (`fr_lint.py`): stages compile/checks/mg5/harness/warn; `FR_SYMBOLS`, `PROTECTED` name sets; `SM_FR = ~/Documents/Github/heptapod/tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr` likely absent in sandbox ⇒ `SM_PARAMS`/`SM_FIELDS_ALL` empty (fewer checks fire); `sm_couplings` set includes `gw`; rules analyzed: `missing_interaction_order`, `undeclared_symbol`, `explicit_flavour_sum`, `majorana_mass_no_half`, `fieldless_term`, `sm_parameter_redeclared` (SM_MASSES hardcoded: MZ,MW,MH,Me,MMU,MTA,MU,MC,MT,MD,MS,MB,WZ,WW,WH,WT — none of our names collide), ParticleName charset (no spaces).
- SM.fr conventions: physical fields `uq,dq,l,vl`; unphysical `QL` (Indices SU2D,Generation,Colour, FlavorIndex SU2D, Y→1/6, Definitions include `CKM[ff,ff2]` for component 2), `uR/dR/lR/LL` (projectors baked in), `Phi` (Y=1/2); params `U1Y,SU2L,SU3C,aEWM1,Gf,aS,ym*,cabi,aEW,MW,sw2,ee,cw,sw,gw,g1,gs,vev,lam,muH,yl,yu,yd,CKM`; `FeynmanGauge = True`; GaugeXi rules present.
- SM.fr Lagrangian idiom (just read): `LGauge := Block[{mu,nu,ii,aa}, ExpandIndices[...]]`, `LFermions := Block[{mu}, ExpandIndices[I*(QLbar.Ga[mu].DC[QL,mu] + ...), FlavorExpand->{SU2W,SU2D}] /. {CKM[a_,b_] Conjugate[CKM[a_,c_]]->IndexDelta[b,c], ...}]`, `LYukawa` builds `yuk` then `yuk+HC[yuk]`. `QLbar.Ga[mu].DC[QL,mu]` spans colour-indexed fields in a dot chain ⇒ Dot contracts colour (supports `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`).

# Mass and width values FeynRules reads: a number, or Internal. The renderer
# also maps "Automatic" to a numeric placeholder. Anything else ("Auto",
# "External", a parameter name) aborts LoadModel with "Wrong width assignment"
# or "Wrong mass assignment", or leaks an undefined name into the UFO.
_MW_WORDS = {"Internal", "Automatic"}
_MW_FUNCS = {"Sqrt", "Pi"}


def check_mass_width_value(v: Optional[str], where: str) -> None:
    if v is None:
        return
    s = str(v).strip()
    if s in _MW_WORDS:
        return
    names = set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z$][A-Za-z0-9$]*", s)) - _MW_FUNCS
    if re.search(r"[0-9.][eE][+-]?[0-9]", s):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{where}: value {s!r} uses e-notation, which Mathematica reads as a "
            "product with a symbol; write it as \"1.*^12\""
        )
    if names or not re.search(r"[0-9]", s) or unbalanced(s):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{where}: value {s!r} is not a number, \"Internal\" or \"Automatic\" "
            "(FeynRules rejects anything else, e.g. \"Auto\" or \"External\"); "

1: """
2: # render.py is a part of the HEPTAPOD package.
3: # Copyright (C) 2025 HEPTAPOD authors (see AUTHORS for details).
4: # HEPTAPOD is licensed under the GNU GPL v3 or later, see LICENSE for details.
5: # Please respect the MCnet Guidelines, see GUIDELINES for details.
6: 
7: Render a validated FeynRulesModel (frmodel.py) to a FeynRules ``.fr`` file.
8: 
9: The fiddly Mathematica syntax (association comma placement, ``->`` vs ``:>``,
10: mass tuples, ``Index[...]`` wrapping, rationals) is built here in tested Python;
11: a thin Jinja2 template (templates/model.fr.j2) supplies the file skeleton.
12: """
13: 
14: from __future__ import annotations
15: 
16: import os
17: from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple
18: 
19: from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape
20: 
21: from .frmodel import (
22:     FeynRulesModel,
23:     GaugeGroup,
24:     IndexDecl,
25:     MassSpec,
26:     Parameter,
27:     ParticleClass,
28: )
29: 
30: _TEMPLATE_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "templates")
31: 
32: 
33: # --------------------------- scalar helpers --------------------------- #
34: 
35: 
36: def _bool(b: bool) -> str:
37:     return "True" if b else "False"
38: 
39: 
40: def _quote(s: str) -> str:
41:     return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
42: 
43: 
44: def _strlist(items: Sequence[str]) -> str:
45:     """M$Information-style: single -> "x"; many -> {"x", "y"}."""
46:     if len(items) == 1:
47:         return _quote(items[0])
48:     return "{" + ", ".join(_quote(x) for x in items) + "}"
49: 
50: 
51: def _name_field(v) -> str:
52:     """ParticleName/FullName/PropagatorLabel: str -> quoted; list -> {...}."""
53:     if isinstance(v, list):
54:         return "{" + ", ".join(_quote(x) for x in v) + "}"
55:     return _quote(v)
56: 
57: 
58: def _pdg(v) -> str:
59:     if isinstance(v, list):
60:         return "{" + ", ".join(str(x) for x in v) + "}"
61:     return str(v)
62: 
63: 
64: def _indices(names: Sequence[str]) -> str:
65:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"Index[{n}]" for n in names) + "}"
66: 
67: 
68: # FeynRules QuantumNumbers holds only additive (U(1)-type) charges. Colour/SU2/
69: # etc. are REPRESENTATION labels fixed by a field's Indices, not quantum numbers;
70: # if left in QuantumNumbers, FeynRules emits an unevaluated `Colour[field]` into
71: # the UFO's particles.py, which MadGraph rejects with "name 'Colour' is not
72: # defined". Drop these reserved index/representation names.
73: _REP_LABELS = {
74:     "Colour", "Color", "Sextet", "Gluon", "Generation", "Spin", "Lorentz",
75:     "SU2", "SU2W", "SU2L", "SU2D", "SU2R",
76: }
77: 
78: 
79: def _additive_qns(d: dict) -> dict:
80:     return {k: v for k, v in d.items() if k not in _REP_LABELS}
81: 
82: 
83: def _reserved_mass_width_names(particles) -> set:
84:     """Mass/width parameter names FeynRules auto-declares from particle Mass/Width
85:     specs. Declaring them again in M$Parameters double-defines the name in the UFO
86:     (MadGraph InvalidModel), so the renderer drops those duplicates."""
87:     names: set = set()
88:     for p in particles or []:
89:         for spec in (getattr(p, "mass", None), getattr(p, "width", None)):
90:             if spec is None:
91:                 continue
92:             if getattr(spec, "sym", None):
93:                 names.add(spec.sym)
94:             for sub, _val in (getattr(spec, "members", None) or []):
95:                 names.add(sub)
96:     return names
97: 
98: 
99: def _is_internal_param(p) -> bool:
100:     """Internal/derived parameters carry a formula (Definitions) that FeynRules
101:     cannot auto-create from a particle Mass/Width spec, so they must stay in
102:     M$Parameters even when named like a mass/width (e.g. a computed decay width
103:     Width -> {WV1, Internal}). Only plain External duplicates are dropped."""
104:     if getattr(p, "definitions", None):
105:         return True
106:     return "internal" in str(getattr(p, "parameter_type", "")).lower()
107: 
108: 
109: def _qn(d: dict) -> str:
110:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"{k} -> {v}" for k, v in _additive_qns(d).items()) + "}"
111: 
112: 
113: def _interaction_order(t: Tuple[str, int]) -> str:
114:     return f"{{{t[0]}, {t[1]}}}"
115: 
116: 
117: def _mw_value(v):
118:     """Normalize a mass/width value. FeynRules' ``Automatic`` width is computed
119:     only when AddDecays is on — which is off for us (broken on Wolfram >=15), so
120:     it leaks the literal ``Automatic`` into the UFO and MadGraph fails with
121:     ``name 'Automatic' is not defined``. Emit a numeric placeholder instead;
122:     MadGraph's compute_widths recovers the real width from the model."""
123:     return "1." if str(v).strip().lower() == "automatic" else v
124: 
125: 
126: def _mass(m: MassSpec) -> str:
127:     if m.massless:
128:         return "0"
129:     if m.members:
130:         parts = [m.sym]
131:         for sub, val in m.members:
132:             val = _mw_value(val)
133:             parts.append(f"{{{sub}, {val}}}" if val is not None else f"{{{sub}}}")
134:         return "{" + ", ".join(parts) + "}"
135:     if m.value is not None:
136:         return f"{{{m.sym}, {_mw_value(m.value)}}}"
137:     return f"{{{m.sym}}}"
138: 
139: 
140: def _reps(reps: Sequence[Tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
141:     if len(reps) == 1:
142:         r, s = reps[0]
143:         return f"{{{r}, {s}}}"
144:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"{{{r}, {s}}}" for r, s in reps) + "}"
145: 
146: 
147: def _assoc(pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]], indent: str = "    ") -> str:
148:     """Render ``{ Key -> val, ... }``, dropping entries whose value is None."""
149:     kept = [(k, v) for k, v in pairs if v is not None]
150:     if not kept:
151:         return "{}"
152:     inner = ",\n".join(f"{indent}{k} -> {v}" for k, v in kept)
153:     close_indent = indent[:-2] if len(indent) >= 2 else ""
154:     return "{\n" + inner + "\n" + close_indent + "}"
155: 
156: 
157: # ------------------------------ blocks ------------------------------- #
158: 
159: 
160: def render_information(info) -> str:
161:     pairs = [
162:         ("Authors", _strlist(info.authors)),
163:         ("Version", _quote(info.version)),
164:         ("Date", _quote(info.date)),
165:         ("Institutions", _strlist(info.institutions) if info.institutions else None),
166:         ("Emails", _strlist(info.emails) if info.emails else None),
167:     ]
168:     return "M$Information = " + _assoc(pairs, indent="  ") + ";"
169: 
170: 
171: def _render_gauge_group(g: GaugeGroup) -> str:
172:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
173:         ("Abelian", _bool(g.abelian)),
174:         ("CouplingConstant", g.coupling_constant),
175:         ("GaugeBoson", g.gauge_boson),
176:         ("Charge", g.charge),
177:         ("StructureConstant", g.structure_constant),
178:         ("Representations", _reps(g.representations) if g.representations else None),
179:         ("SymmetricTensor", g.symmetric_tensor),
180:         (
181:             "Definitions",
182:             ("{" + ", ".join(g.definitions) + "}") if g.definitions else None,
183:         ),
184:     ]
185:     return f"  {g.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
186: 
187: 
188: def render_gauge_groups(groups: List[GaugeGroup]) -> str:
189:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_gauge_group(g) for g in groups)
190:     return "M$GaugeGroups = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
191: 
192: 
193: def render_index_decls(decls: List[IndexDecl]) -> str:
194:     lines: List[str] = []
195:     for d in decls:
196:         if d.range_kind.value == "Range":
197:             rng = f"Range[{d.size}]"
198:         else:
199:             rng = f"{d.range_kind.value}[Range[{d.size}]]"
200:         lines.append(f"IndexRange[Index[{d.name}]] = {rng};")
201:     for d in decls:
202:         if d.style_symbol:
203:             lines.append(f"IndexStyle[{d.name}, {d.style_symbol}];")
204:     return "\n".join(lines)
205: 
206: 
207: def _render_parameter(p: Parameter) -> str:
208:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
209:         ("ParameterType", p.parameter_type.value if p.parameter_type else None),
210:     ]
211:     if p.is_tensor:
212:         pairs.append(
213:             (
214:                 "Value",
215:                 ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.value_rules) + "}")
216:                 if p.value_rules
217:                 else None,
218:             )
219:         )
220:         pairs.append(("Indices", _indices(p.indices)))
221:     else:
222:         pairs.append(("Value", p.value))
223:     pairs += [
224:         ("ComplexParameter", _bool(p.complex) if p.complex is not None else None),
225:         ("BlockName", p.block_name),
226:         ("OrderBlock", str(p.order_block) if p.order_block is not None else None),
227:         (
228:             "InteractionOrder",
229:             _interaction_order(p.interaction_order) if p.interaction_order else None,
230:         ),
231:         (
232:             "Definitions",
233:             ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.definitions) + "}")
234:             if p.definitions
235:             else None,
236:         ),
237:         ("ParameterName", p.parameter_name),
238:         ("TensorClass", p.tensor_class),
239:         ("Unitary", _bool(p.unitary) if p.unitary is not None else None),
240:         ("Hermitian", _bool(p.hermitian) if p.hermitian is not None else None),
241:         ("Orthogonal", _bool(p.orthogonal) if p.orthogonal is not None else None),
242:         (
243:             "AllowSummation",
244:             _bool(p.allow_summation) if p.allow_summation is not None else None,
245:         ),
246:         # TeX is a LaTeX label; render it as a quoted Mathematica string with
247:         # backslashes escaped ("\\Gamma_U"), else a raw value like \Gamma_U is a
248:         # Mathematica syntax error that aborts the whole M$Parameters block.
249:         ("TeX", _quote(p.tex) if p.tex else None),
250:         ("Description", _quote(p.description) if p.description else None),
251:     ]
252:     return f"  {p.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
253: 
254: 
255: def render_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> str:
256:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_parameter(p) for p in params)
257:     return "M$Parameters = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
258: 
259: 
260: def _render_particle(p: ParticleClass) -> str:
261:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
262:         ("ClassName", p.class_name),
263:         ("SelfConjugate", _bool(p.self_conjugate)),
264:         (
265:             "ClassMembers",
266:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.class_members) + "}") if p.class_members else None,
267:         ),
268:         ("Indices", _indices(p.indices) if p.indices else None),
269:         ("FlavorIndex", p.flavor_index),
270:         ("Mass", _mass(p.mass) if p.mass else None),
271:         ("Width", _mass(p.width) if p.width else None),
272:         ("QuantumNumbers",
273:          _qn(p.quantum_numbers) if _additive_qns(p.quantum_numbers or {}) else None),
274:         ("PDG", _pdg(p.pdg) if p.pdg is not None else None),
275:         ("ParticleName", _name_field(p.particle_name) if p.particle_name else None),
276:         (
277:             "AntiParticleName",
278:             _name_field(p.antiparticle_name) if p.antiparticle_name else None,
279:         ),
280:         ("FullName", _name_field(p.full_name) if p.full_name else None),
281:         (
282:             "PropagatorLabel",
283:             _name_field(p.propagator_label) if p.propagator_label else None,
284:         ),
285:         ("PropagatorType", p.propagator_type.value if p.propagator_type else None),
286:         ("PropagatorArrow", p.propagator_arrow.value if p.propagator_arrow else None),
287:         ("Ghost", p.ghost),
288:         ("Goldstone", p.goldstone),
289:         ("Chirality", p.chirality),
290:         ("MajoranaPhase", p.majorana_phase),
291:         (
292:             "WeylComponents",
293:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.weyl_components) + "}") if p.weyl_components else None,
294:         ),
295:         ("Unphysical", _bool(True) if p.unphysical else None),
296:         (
297:             "Definitions",
298:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.definitions) + "}") if p.definitions else None,
299:         ),
300:     ]
301:     return f"  {p.class_label} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
302: 
303: 
304: def render_classes(particles: List[ParticleClass]) -> str:
305:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_particle(p) for p in particles)
306:     return "M$ClassesDescription = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
307: 
308: 
309: def render_model(model: FeynRulesModel) -> str:
310:     """Render a validated FeynRulesModel to a complete ``.fr`` string."""
311:     sections: List[str] = [render_information(model.info)]
312: 
313:     if model.interaction_order_hierarchy:
314:         ih = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_hierarchy)
315:         sections.append("M$InteractionOrderHierarchy = {" + ih + "};")
316:     if model.interaction_order_limit:
317:         il = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_limit)
318:         sections.append("M$InteractionOrderLimit = {" + il + "};")
319:     if model.feynman_gauge is not None:
320:         sections.append(f"FeynmanGauge = {_bool(model.feynman_gauge)};")
321:     if model.vevs:
322:         vv = ", ".join(f"{{{f}, {v}}}" for f, v in model.vevs)
323:         sections.append("M$vevs = {" + vv + "};")
324: 
325:     for raw in model.raw_preamble:
326:         sections.append(raw)
327: 
328:     if model.index_decls:
329:         sections.append(render_index_decls(model.index_decls))
330:     if model.gauge_groups:
331:         sections.append(render_gauge_groups(model.gauge_groups))
332:     if model.parameters:
333:         # FeynRules auto-declares the mass/width parameters named in each
334:         # particle's Mass/Width spec. Re-declaring them in M$Parameters makes the
335:         # UFO define the name twice, which MadGraph rejects ("name X define
336:         # multiple time"). Drop those duplicates; keep genuine couplings.
337:         reserved = _reserved_mass_width_names(model.particles)
338:         params = [p for p in model.parameters
339:                   if p.name not in reserved or _is_internal_param(p)]
340:         if params:
341:             sections.append(render_parameters(params))
342:     if model.particles:
343:         sections.append(render_classes(model.particles))
344:     for field, expr in model.gauge_xi:
345:         sections.append(f"GaugeXi[{field}] = {expr};")
346: 
347:     for raw in model.raw_blocks:
348:         sections.append(raw)
349: 
350:     for t in model.lagrangian_terms:
351:         op = ":=" if t.delayed else "="
352:         # Defensive: some (LLM-produced) expressions already carry a leading
353:         # assignment operator ("= ..." or ":= ..."); strip it so we don't emit a
354:         # duplicated operator (e.g. "L := := Block[...]").
355:         rhs = t.expression.lstrip()
356:         for lead in (":=", "="):
357:             if rhs.startswith(lead):
358:                 rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
359:                 break
360:         sections.append(f"{t.name} {op} {rhs};")
361: 
362:     env = Environment(
363:         loader=FileSystemLoader(_TEMPLATE_DIR),
364:         autoescape=select_autoescape(enabled_extensions=(), default=False),
365:         keep_trailing_newline=True,
366:     )
367:     template = env.get_template("model.fr.j2")
368:     return template.render(model_name=model.model_name, body="\n\n".join(sections))

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.
3: 
4: Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
5: MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
6: repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
7: predicts takes up to 900 s.
8: 
9: Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
10:   compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
11:   checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
12:   mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
13:   harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
14:   warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass
15: 
16: Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: import json
22: import re
23: import sys
24: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
25: from pathlib import Path
26: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
27: 
28: HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
29: SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"
30: 
31: # Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
32: # not be named after (rule 10).
33: FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
34:               "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
35:               "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
36: PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
37:              "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
38:              "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}
39: 
40: # Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
41: _SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
42: SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
43: SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
44: for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
45:     SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
46: _i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
47: SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
48: SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
49: SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
50:               "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
51: SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}

77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:

81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue

85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:

90:         elif text[i] == "\n":

96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]

120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""

129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)

154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:

274: \section{Effective Left-Right Symmetric Model}\label{sec:theory}
275: The Effective LRSM field content consists of the usual SM states, the $\WR^\pm$ and $\ZR$ gauge bosons, 
276: which are aligned with their mass eigenstates, and three heavy Majorana neutrinos $N_i$, 
277: aligned with the RH chiral states.
278: 
279: In the LRSM, the $\WR$ chiral coupling to quarks are given by
280: \begin{eqnarray}
281:  \mathcal{L}_{\WR-q-q'} = \frac{-\kappa_R^q g}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{i,j=u,d,\dots}\overline{u}_i V_{ij}^{\rm CKM'}~W_{R \mu}^+ \gamma^\mu P_R~ d_j + \text{H.c.},
282:  \label{chcurrent}
283: \end{eqnarray}
284: Here, $u_i (d_j)$ is an up-(down-)type quark of flavor $i (j)$; 
285: $P_{R(L)} = \frac{1}{2}(1\pm\gamma^5)$ denotes the RH(LH) chiral projection operator; and
286: $V_{ij}^{\rm CKM'}$  is the RH Cabbibo-Kobayashi-Masakawa (CKM) matrix, which is related to the SM CKM matrix.
287: Throughout this study, we will assume five massless quarks and take both the SM and RH CKM matrices to be diagonal with unit entries.
288: $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha_{\rm EM}(M_Z)}/\sin\theta_W$ is the SM Weak coupling constant and 
289: $\kappa_{R}^{q}\in\mathds{R}$ is an overall normalization for the $\WR$ interaction strength.
290: 
291: For leptons, the $\WR$ coupling and leptonic mixing is parametrized by~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Han:2012vk}
292: \begin{eqnarray}
293:  \mathcal{L}_{\WR-\ell-\nu/N} = \frac{-\kappa_R^\ell g}{\sqrt{2}}
294:  \sum_{\ell=e,\mu,\tau}
295:  \left[
296:  \sum_{m=1}^3	\overline{\nu^{c}_m} X_{\ell m} ~+~
297:  \sum_{m'=1}^3	\overline{N_{m'}} Y_{\ell m'}
298:  \right] ~W_{R \mu}^+ \gamma^\mu P_R~ \ell^-+\text{H.c.}
299: \end{eqnarray}
300: The matrix $Y_{\ell m'} (X_{\ell m})$ quantifies the mixing between 
301: the heavy (light) neutrino mass eigenstate $N_{m'}~(\nu_{m})$
302: and the RH chiral state with corresponding lepton flavor $\ell$. 
303: 
304: The mixing scale as~\cite{Keung:1983uu}
305: \begin{equation}
306: \vert Y_{\ell m'}\vert^2 \sim \mathcal{O}(1) \quad\text{and}\quad  
307: \vert X_{\ell m}\vert^2 \sim 1 - \vert Y_{\ell m'}\vert^2 \sim \mathcal{O}(m_{\nu_m}/m_{N_{m'}}).
308: \end{equation}
309: As in the quark sector, $\kappa_R^\ell\in\mathds{R}$ independently normalizes the $\WR$ coupling strength to leptons.
310: 
311: At TeV collider scales, both light neutrino masses and light neutrino mixing can be taken to zero.
312: So for simplicity, we take $Y_{\ell m'}$ to  be diagonal with unit entires:
313: \begin{equation}
314:   \vert Y_{e N}\vert = \vert Y_{\mu N_2}\vert = \vert Y_{\tau N_3}\vert = 1, \quad \vert Y_{\rm others}\vert = \vert X_{\ell m}\vert = 0.
315:   \label{eq:lrsmNuMixing}
316: \end{equation}
317: 
318: Mass and mixing assumptions are modifiable in the public model files~\cite{nloFRModel} but requires UFO regeneration.
319: Specifically, do not load the FR restrictions, ``massless.rst'' and ``diagonalCKM.rst''.
320: 
321:

344: 
345: After LR symmetry breaking, the $W_{R}^{3}$ and $X_{(B-L)}$ gauge states mix and
346: give rise to the massive $Z_{R}$ and massless (hypercharge) $B$ bosons.
347: 
348: Subsequently, all fermions with $(B-L)$ charges, including $\nu_L$ and $N_R$, couple to $\ZR$.
349: 
350: For chiral fermion $f$, we parametrize the $\ZR$ neutral currents by
351: \begin{eqnarray}
352:  \mathcal{L}_{\ZR-f-f} &=& \frac{-\kappa_{R}^f g}{\sqrt{1 - \left(1/\kappa_{R}^f\right)^2\tWSq}}\sum_{f=u,e,\dots}
353:  \overline{f} Z_{R \mu} \gamma^\mu \left(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}P_L + g_{R}^{\ZR,f}P_R\right)f.
354: \label{neucurrent}
355: \end{eqnarray}
356: $\kappa_{R}^{f}$ are the same $\kappa_{R}^{q,\ell}$ as for $\WR$.
357: In terms of electric and isospin charges, the chiral coefficients are
358: \begin{eqnarray}
359:  g_{L}^{\ZR,f} &=& \left(T_{L}^{3,f} - Q^f\right)\frac{1}{\kappa_{R}^{f~2}}\tWSq,
360:  \\
361:  g_{R}^{\ZR,f} &=& T_{R}^{3,f} - \frac{1}{\kappa_{R}^{f~2}}\tWSq Q^f.
362: \end{eqnarray}
363: SU$(2)_L$, SU$(2)_R$, and U$(1)_{\rm EM}$ quantum number assignments for $f$ are summarize in Tbl.~\ref{tb:qNumbers}.
364: 
365: For generic $\kappa_R^{q,\ell}$ normalizations, the LO $\WR,\ZR$ partial decay widths are then
366: \begin{eqnarray}
367:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow q\overline{q'}} 	&=& N_c \vert V^{\rm{CKM'}}_{qq'}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{q 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
368:  \\
369:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow tb} 	&=& N_c \vert V^{\rm{CKM'}}_{tb}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{q 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
370: 					    \left(1-r_t^{\WR}\right)^2\left(1+\frac{1}{2}r_t^{\WR}\right),
371:  \\
372:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow \ell N_{m'}} 	&=&     \vert Y_{\ell N_{m'}}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{\ell 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
373: 					\left(1-r_N^{\WR}\right)^2\left(1+\frac{1}{2}r_N^{\WR}\right),
374: \\
375:  \Gam{\ZR\rightarrow f\overline{f}} &=&   
376:  N_c^f 
377:  \cfrac{\kappa_{\ZR}^{f 2} g^2 \MZR \sqrt{1-4r_f^{\ZR}}}{48\pi\left[1 - (1/\kappa_{R}^f)^2\tWSq\right]}
378:  \nonumber\\
379:  &\times&
380:  \left[(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}+g_{R}^{\ZR,f})^2(1+2r_f^{\ZR})+(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}-g_{R}^{\ZR,f})^2(1-4r_f^{\ZR})\right]
381:  \\
382:  r_i^{V_R} &=& \frac{m_{i}^2}{M_{V_R}^2}.
383: \end{eqnarray}
384: Assuming diagonal quark mixing and lepton mixing in Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmNuMixing}), the total $\WR,\ZR$ widths are then
385: \begin{eqnarray}
386:  \Gamma_{\WR} &=& 2\Gam{\WR \rightarrow q\overline{q'}} + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow tb} 
387:  + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow e N_{1}} + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow \mu N_{2}} + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow \tau N_{3}}
388:  \\
389:  \Gamma_{\ZR} &=& \sum_{f} \Gam{\ZR\rightarrow f\overline{f}}
390: \end{eqnarray}

class FeynRulesModel(BaseModel):
    """A complete FeynRules ``.fr`` model, ready to render."""

    model_name: str
    info: ModelInfo
    interaction_order_hierarchy: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    interaction_order_limit: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    feynman_gauge: Optional[bool] = None
    vevs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # {{Phi[..], vev}}
    gauge_groups: List[GaugeGroup] = []
    index_decls: List[IndexDecl] = []
    parameters: List[Parameter] = []
    particles: List[ParticleClass] = []
    gauge_xi: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (V[3], "GaugeXi[W]")
    lagrangian_terms: List[LagrangianTerm] = []
    # Verbatim escape hatches for irregular constructs (FR$LoopSwitches,
    # Mix[...] mixing blocks, SUSY superfields, ...).
    raw_preamble: List[str] = []  # emitted after M$Information, before IndexRange
    raw_blocks: List[str] = []  # emitted just before Lagrangian terms

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "FeynRulesModel":
        labels = [p.class_label for p in self.particles]
        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
            dupes = sorted({x for x in labels if labels.count(x) > 1})
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate ParticleClass labels: {dupes}")

        # Lorentz/Spin* are FeynRules built-ins. Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/
        # SU2W are declared by SM.fr, which every BSM add-on is loaded on top of,
        # so they need no IndexRange in the add-on itself (matches the reference
        # S1_LQ_RR.fr, which uses Index[Colour] without redeclaring it). Only
        # genuinely new indices must be declared in index_decls.
        builtin = {
            "Lorentz", "Spin", "Spin1", "Spin2",
            "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation", "SU2D", "SU2W",
        }
        declared = {d.name for d in self.index_decls} | builtin
        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
        }
        missing = used - declared
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"
            )

        for i, raw in enumerate(self.raw_preamble):
            _require_balanced(raw, f"raw_preamble[{i}]")
        for i, raw in enumerate(self.raw_blocks):
            _require_balanced(raw, f"raw_blocks[{i}]")

        names = [p.name for p in self.parameters]
        dupes = sorted({x for x in names if names.count(x) > 1})
        if dupes:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate parameter names: {dupes}")
        sizes = dict(_INDEX_SIZE, **{d.name: d.size for d in self.index_decls})
        _check_block_collisions(self.parameters, sizes)

        self.parameters = topo_sort_parameters(self.parameters)
        return self

class Rule(BaseModel):
    """One Mathematica replacement rule, e.g. ``CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi]``."""

    lhs: str
    rhs: str
    delayed: bool = False  # False -> "->", True -> ":>"

    def render(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.lhs} {':>' if self.delayed else '->'} {self.rhs}"

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "Rule":
        _require_balanced(self.lhs, f"rule lhs {self.lhs[:40]!r}")
        _require_balanced(self.rhs, f"rule {self.lhs[:40]!r} rhs")
        return self


class ParamType(str, Enum):
    External = "External"
    Internal = "Internal"


class SpinType(str, Enum):
    S = "S"  # scalar
    F = "F"  # fermion
    V = "V"  # vector
    U = "U"  # ghost
    T = "T"  # tensor
    W = "W"  # Weyl fermion
    R = "R"  # spin-3/2
    RW = "RW"


class RangeKind(str, Enum):
    Unfold = "Unfold"
    NoUnfold = "NoUnfold"
    Range = "Range"


class PropType(str, Enum):
    Sine = "Sine"
    Straight = "Straight"
    ScalarDash = "ScalarDash"
    GhostDash = "GhostDash"
    Curly = "Curly"
    W = "W"
    C = "C"
    S = "S"
    D = "D"


class PropArrow(str, Enum):
    true = "True"
    false = "False"
    none = "None"
    forward = "Forward"


class ModelInfo(BaseModel):
    authors: List[str]
    version: str
    date: str
    institutions: List[str] = []
    emails: List[str] = []


class GaugeGroup(BaseModel):
    """A M$GaugeGroups entry. Omitted entirely by BSM add-on models."""

    name: str  # LHS symbol: U1Y, SU2L, SU3C
    abelian: bool
    gauge_boson: str
    coupling_constant: Optional[str] = None
    charge: Optional[str] = None  # required iff abelian
    structure_constant: Optional[str] = None  # required iff non-abelian
    symmetric_tensor: Optional[str] = None
    representations: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # [("T","Colour")] or many
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM rule strings

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "GaugeGroup":
        if self.abelian and not self.charge:
            raise ValueError(f"gauge group {self.name}: Abelian group needs charge")
        if not self.abelian and not self.structure_constant:
            raise ValueError(
                f"gauge group {self.name}: non-Abelian group needs structure_constant"
            )
        for d in self.definitions:
            _require_balanced(d, f"gauge group {self.name} definition")
        return self


class IndexDecl(BaseModel):
    name: str  # Colour, Generation, SU2W ...
    range_kind: RangeKind
    size: int  # Range[size]
    style_symbol: Optional[str] = None  # IndexStyle[name, style_symbol]


class Parameter(BaseModel):
    """A M$Parameters entry (LHS symbol of ``==``)."""

    name: str
    parameter_type: Optional[ParamType] = None
    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # scalar; tensors use value_rules
    value_rules: List[Rule] = []  # tensor Value -> { ... }
    complex: Optional[bool] = None  # ComplexParameter
    block_name: Optional[str] = None  # External only
    order_block: Optional[int] = None  # External SCALAR only
    interaction_order: Optional[Tuple[str, int]] = None  # -> {NP, 1}
    indices: List[str] = []  # non-empty => tensor
    definitions: List[Rule] = []
    parameter_name: Optional[str] = None
    tex: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    tensor_class: Optional[str] = None
    # tensor-only flags
    unitary: Optional[bool] = None
    hermitian: Optional[bool] = None
    orthogonal: Optional[bool] = None
    allow_summation: Optional[bool] = None

def _render_parameter(p: Parameter) -> str:
    pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
        ("ParameterType", p.parameter_type.value if p.parameter_type else None),
    ]
    if p.is_tensor:
        pairs.append(
            (
                "Value",
                ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.value_rules) + "}")
                if p.value_rules
                else None,
            )
        )
        pairs.append(("Indices", _indices(p.indices)))
    else:
        pairs.append(("Value", p.value))
    pairs += [
        ("ComplexParameter", _bool(p.complex) if p.complex is not None else None),
        ("BlockName", p.block_name),
        ("OrderBlock", str(p.order_block) if p.order_block is not None else None),
        (
            "InteractionOrder",
            _interaction_order(p.interaction_order) if p.interaction_order else None,
        ),
        (
            "Definitions",
            ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.definitions) + "}")
            if p.definitions
            else None,
        ),
        ("ParameterName", p.parameter_name),
        ("TensorClass", p.tensor_class),
        ("Unitary", _bool(p.unitary) if p.unitary is not None else None),
        ("Hermitian", _bool(p.hermitian) if p.hermitian is not None else None),
        ("Orthogonal", _bool(p.orthogonal) if p.orthogonal is not None else None),
        (
            "AllowSummation",
            _bool(p.allow_summation) if p.allow_summation is not None else None,
        ),
        # TeX is a LaTeX label; render it as a quoted Mathematica string with
        # backslashes escaped ("\\Gamma_U"), else a raw value like \Gamma_U is a
        # Mathematica syntax error that aborts the whole M$Parameters block.
        ("TeX", _quote(p.tex) if p.tex else None),
        ("Description", _quote(p.description) if p.description else None),
    ]
    return f"  {p.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")


def render_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> str:
    entries = ",\n".join(_render_parameter(p) for p in params)
    return "M$Parameters = {\n" + entries + "\n};"


def _render_particle(p: ParticleClass) -> str:
    pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
        ("ClassName", p.class_name),
        ("SelfConjugate", _bool(p.self_conjugate)),
        (
            "ClassMembers",
            ("{" + ", ".join(p.class_members) + "}") if p.class_members else None,
        ),
        ("Indices", _indices(p.indices) if p.indices else None),
        ("FlavorIndex", p.flavor_index),
        ("Mass", _mass(p.mass) if p.mass else None),
        ("Width", _mass(p.width) if p.width else None),
        ("QuantumNumbers",
         _qn(p.quantum_numbers) if _additive_qns(p.quantum_numbers or {}) else None),
        ("PDG", _pdg(p.pdg) if p.pdg is not None else None),
        ("ParticleName", _name_field(p.particle_name) if p.particle_name else None),
        (
            "AntiParticleName",
            _name_field(p.antiparticle_name) if p.antiparticle_name else None,
        ),
        ("FullName", _name_field(p.full_name) if p.full_name else None),
        (
            "PropagatorLabel",
            _name_field(p.propagator_label) if p.propagator_label else None,
        ),
        ("PropagatorType", p.propagator_type.value if p.propagator_type else None),
        ("PropagatorArrow", p.propagator_arrow.value if p.propagator_arrow else None),
        ("Ghost", p.ghost),
        ("Goldstone", p.goldstone),
        ("Chirality", p.chirality),
        ("MajoranaPhase", p.majorana_phase),
        (
            "WeylComponents",
            ("{" + ", ".join(p.weyl_components) + "}") if p.weyl_components else None,
        ),
        ("Unphysical", _bool(True) if p.unphysical else None),
        (
            "Definitions",
            ("{" + ", ".join(p.definitions) + "}") if p.definitions else None,
        ),
    ]
    return f"  {p.class_label} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")


def render_classes(particles: List[ParticleClass]) -> str:
    entries = ",\n".join(_render_particle(p) for p in particles)
    return "M$ClassesDescription = {\n" + entries + "\n};"


def render_model(model: FeynRulesModel) -> str:
    """Render a validated FeynRulesModel to a complete ``.fr`` string."""
    sections: List[str] = [render_information(model.info)]

    if model.interaction_order_hierarchy:
        ih = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_hierarchy)
        sections.append("M$InteractionOrderHierarchy = {" + ih + "};")
    if model.interaction_order_limit:
        il = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_limit)
        sections.append("M$InteractionOrderLimit = {" + il + "};")
    if model.feynman_gauge is not None:
        sections.append(f"FeynmanGauge = {_bool(model.feynman_gauge)};")
    if model.vevs:
        vv = ", ".join(f"{{{f}, {v}}}" for f, v in model.vevs)
        sections.append("M$vevs = {" + vv + "};")

    for raw in model.raw_preamble:
        sections.append(raw)

    if model.index_decls:
        sections.append(render_index_decls(model.index_decls))
    if model.gauge_groups:
        sections.append(render_gauge_groups(model.gauge_groups))
    if model.parameters:
        # FeynRules auto-declares the mass/width parameters named in each
        # particle's Mass/Width spec. Re-declaring them in M$Parameters makes the
        # UFO define the name twice, which MadGraph rejects ("name X define
        # multiple time"). Drop those duplicates; keep genuine couplings.
        reserved = _reserved_mass_width_names(model.particles)
        params = [p for p in model.parameters
                  if p.name not in reserved or _is_internal_param(p)]
        if params:
            sections.append(render_parameters(params))
    if model.particles:
        sections.append(render_classes(model.particles))
    for field, expr in model.gauge_xi:
        sections.append(f"GaugeXi[{field}] = {expr};")

    for raw in model.raw_blocks:
        sections.append(raw)

    for t in model.lagrangian_terms:
        op = ":=" if t.delayed else "="
        # Defensive: some (LLM-produced) expressions already carry a leading
        # assignment operator ("= ..." or ":= ..."); strip it so we don't emit a
        # duplicated operator (e.g. "L := := Block[...]").
        rhs = t.expression.lstrip()
        for lead in (":=", "="):
            if rhs.startswith(lead):
                rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
                break

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
predicts takes up to 900 s.

Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
  compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
  checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
  mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
  harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
  warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass

Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set

HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"

# Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
# not be named after (rule 10).
FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
              "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
              "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
             "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
             "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}

# Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
_SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
    SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
_i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
              "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}
SM_MASSES = {"MZ", "MW", "MH", "Me", "MMU", "MTA", "MU", "MC", "MT", "MD", "MS", "MB",
             "WZ", "WW", "WH", "WT"}

FR_BUILTINS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
               "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos",
               "Tan", "I", "Pi", "Sum", "Block", "Module", "ExpandIndices",
               "FlavorExpand", "True", "False", "bar", "anti", "left", "right",
               "Conjugate", "Re", "Im", "Abs", "Sig", "Ta", "T6", "K6", "K6bar",
               "K3", "K3bar", "f", "dSUN", "Dot", "Times", "Plus", "Power",
               "Automatic", "Internal", "External", "Unfold", "NoUnfold", "Range",
               "Index", "Lorentz", "Spin", "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation",
               "SU2D", "SU2W", "Sextet", "IndexStyle", "MakeIdenticalFermions",
               "Expand", "Simplify", "ProjPlus", "ProjMinus", "FR$", "vev"}


@dataclass
class Finding:
    rule: str
    stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn

## Objective
- Extract the complete new-physics content of the EffLRSM model (arXiv:1610.08985) from its LaTeX source into a `spec.json` FeynRulesModel object, run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate until valid.
- Final deliverable: a message containing the self-audit tab (format per TASK.md); `spec.json` written in the current directory.

## Important Details
- Working directory: `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-EffLRSM-5kxupzbf/` (stay inside it). Bash DENIED except `./frgen *` (deny rule confirmed in tool error); use `glob`/`read`/`write`. Reads truncate at 2000 chars/line and by line limit — read in chunks.
- External paths DENIED: `benchmarks/open_bench/frgen_cli.py` (real CLI the `./frgen` wrapper execs) unreadable — infer usage only from TASK.md.
- `./frgen` wrapper (root `frgen`, 2 lines): `FRGEN_TOOLKIT="$(pwd)/tools" exec "<venv>/bin/python" ".../benchmarks/open_bench/frgen_cli.py" "$@"`. `tools/frgen/__init__.py` empty.
- Model name must be `"EffLRSM_gen"`; JSON only in `spec.json`.
- Schema: numeric physics values are STRINGS (`"-1/3"`, `"3000."`, `"1.*^12"`, `"2.12*^-8"`); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups: []`; standard indices (Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W) need no declaration; unique `class_index`; `self_conjugate=true` for real/Majorana; no QuantumNumbers on self-conjugate fields (lint `selfconjugate_with_qn`); unique class labels (FeynRulesModel duplicate-label check); `InteractionOrder {NP,1}` on new coupling params with hierarchy `{{"QCD",1},{"QED",2},{"NP",1}}`; completeness scored; `LTotal` must be the total term.
- TASK.md is 91 lines, fully read; self-audit tab format in its tail (rule 84: use charges declared in `QuantumNumbers` + SM.fr charges for SM fields; every Q, Y, new-U(1) sum must be 0; lepton/baryon number is a separate reported column, not required to vanish).
- Paper structure mapped: theory §2 lines 274–430, constraints 431, limits 454, setup 478–535, results 560+, appendix 1017+; lines 498–1736 verified to contain only MC setup/results/references — no extra model content.

### Model content extracted from paper (verified)
- New particles: `WR` complex vector, mass `"3000."`, width `"84.3"`, **`QuantumNumbers -> {Q -> 1}` only (no Y — corrected decision, see below)**; `ZR` real self-conjugate vector, mass `"5070."`, width `"114."`, no QNs; Majorana class `NR` members `N1,N2,N3` (self-conjugate, no QNs; masses `"173.3"`, `"1.*^12"`, `"1.*^12"`; WN1 `"2.12*^-8"`, wn2/wn3 placeholder `"1."`). `N` is protected ⇒ never a bare class name. New width params avoid SM's `WW`/`WZ` ⇒ `WWR`, `WZR`.
- Mass/Width symbols (FR auto-declares them ⇒ do NOT list them in `parameters`; render drops them via `_reserved_mass_width_names`): `MWR`/`WWR`, `MZR`/`WZR`, and for NR `Mass -> {Mn, {mn1, 173.3}, {mn2, 1.*^12}, {mn3, 1.*^12}}` (member entries are `{massParamName, value}`, matched positionally — proven by SM.fr `Mass -> {Ml, {Me,5.11*^-4}, {MMU,0.10566}, {MTA,1.777}}`). Paper's MG commands `set MWR` (line 1032), `set mn1` (1067-1068) ⇒ symbol names `MWR`, `mn1/mn2/mn3` are correct.
- SM.fr Mass/Width forms confirmed: class sym first for Mass (`{Ml, {Me,v},...}`), Width may be a per-member list with no class sym (`Width -> {0, 0, {WT,1.50833649}}` for uq) or `{WZ, 2.4952}` single. `MassSpec.members` in schema requires `sym` and renders `{sym, {sub, val}, ...}` ⇒ NR member subs = `mn1,mn2,mn3`.
- Charged-vector symbol RESOLVED: from `Wi[mu,1] -> (Wbar+W)/Sqrt[2]`, `Wi[mu,2] -> (Wbar-W)/(I Sqrt[2])` and `W^± = (W^1 ∓ iW^2)/√2` ⇒ **`W` = W+**. So write `WR[mu]` (Q→1 field) in charged currents, not `WRbar`.
- ParticleName: lint `bad_particle_name` charset `[\'`\s!@#%^&*()=\[\]{}|\;:<>?/,]` excludes `+`/`-`/`~`; SM.fr uses `"W+"` ⇒ `"WR+"/"WR-"` (or lowercase) is valid; task rule 10 only bans primes like `W'`.
- Gauge groups (SM.fr lines 66-89): `U1Y {Abelian, CouplingConstant -> g1, GaugeBoson -> B, Charge -> Y}`, `SU2L {gw, Wi, Eps, {Ta,SU2D}}`, `SU3C {gs, G, f, {T,Colour}, dSUN}`; IndexRange/Style lines 96-106 (`IndexStyle[Generation, f]`); interaction-order section starts line 110.
- SM.fr QuantumNumbers convention (confirmed by reads of lines 340-395): unphysical multiplets declare **only Y** (`LL -1/2`, `lR -1`, `QL 1/6`, `uR 2/3`, `dR -1/3`, `Phi 1/2`); physical fields (`vl,l,uq,dq`) declare **only Q** (`l` `{Q->-1, LeptonNumber->1}`, `uq` `{Q->2/3}`) and no Y. Declared Y satisfies `Q = T3L + Y` and equals `Y_LR = T3R+(B−L)/2` for SM fermions (also = Y_weak/2).
- **Corrected charge decision:** WR declares `{Q -> 1}` ONLY (mirroring SM `W`). Rationale: with `uq/dq/l` carrying no Y, declaring `Y->1` on WR makes the declared Y sum = 1 ≠ 0, violating TASK rule 84. Physical chiral check still gives 0 (report in audit): LWRqq `ū_R −2/3 + d_R −1/3 + WR +1 = 0`; LWRlnu `N̄ Y=0 + ℓ_R −1 + WR +1 = 0` ⇒ **Y(N)=0, Y(ZR)=0, Y(WR)=+1** (all ZR vertices trivially 0).
- Q sums verified 0 for every term: LWRqq `−2/3 −1/3 +1=0`; LWRlnu `0 −1 +1=0`; ZR terms with `uq,dq,l,vl,NR` all 0; kinetic terms `−1+1=0`.
- Lepton number: NR carries none (Majorana ⇒ no QNs) so LWRlnu declared L sum = +1; report in audit as the expected Majorana L-violation (only Q/Y/new-U(1) sums are required to be 0).
- Chirality: `N̄ γ^μ P_R ℓ = N̄_R γ^μ ℓ_R` ⇒ render `NRbar.yN.Ga[mu].ProjP.l`; Y_LR(ℓ_R) = −1 ⇒ Y(N) = 0 consistent.
- **Dot contraction model resolved:** flavour indices contract between flavour-carrying factors in sequence, non-flavour factors (Ga, ProjP) transparent — consistent with TASK rule 13 idioms `LLbar.yN.NR`, `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`, `ISbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.IS` ⇒ `NRbar.yN.Ga[mu].ProjP.l` and `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq` are correct; no explicit-index forms.
- Paper equations (verbatim, lines 274–403): quark current `-κ_R^q g/√2 Σ ū_i V^{CKM'}_ij W_R^+ γ^μ P_R d_j + H.c.` (line 281); lepton current line 293 `-κ_R^ℓ g/√2 Σ_ℓ [Σ_{m=1}^3 ν̄^c_m X_{ℓm} + Σ_{m'} N̄_{m'} Y_{ℓm'}] W_R^+ γ^μ P_R ℓ^- + H.c.`; ZR line 352 `-κ_R^f g/Sqrt[1-(1/κ_R^f)² tan²θW] Σ_f ...`, `g_L=(T3L−Q)tan²θW/κ²` (359), `g_R=T3R−tan²θW·Q/κ²` (361); widths 367–377; benchmark line 419 `MWR=3 TeV, m_N1=m_t=173.3 GeV, m_N2,m_N3=10^12 GeV`; macros `\tWSq`=tan²θW (86), `\MWR` (64), `\MZR` (65).
- Benchmark X_{ℓm}=0 ⇒ drop `ν̄^c X` term (avoids `CC[...]`); no mixing; +HC on both WR currents only, no HC on ZR terms.
- Derived chiral coefficients (t = tan²θW): `gZLq = -(1/6) t/kappaRq^2`; `gZRu = 1/2-(2/3) t/kappaRq^2`; `gZRd = -1/2+(1/3) t/kappaRq^2`; `gZLl = (1/2) t/kappaRl^2`; `gZRe = -1/2 + t/kappaRl^2`; `gZRN = 1/2`; ZR prefactors inline (`-kappaRq gw/Sqrt[1-tan2thetaW/kappaRq^2]`, leptons with `kappaRl`).

Γ(ZR), t=0.30083, g²=0.4246, MZR=5070: u 11.30, d/s/b 19.89 ⇒ u+d+s+c+b 82.27 ✓(82.3); tt 11.30 ✓; ℓ×3 7.63 ✓(7.64); light ν×3 2.77 ✓(2.78); N1N1 (Majorana, g_R=1/2) 10.21 ✓(10.2); total 114.2 ✓(114). Decision: `tan2thetaW = sw2/(1-sw2)` using SM.sw2.

Names containing `kin` are skipped by lint `missing_interaction_order`.

168: \section{Introduction}
169: The Left Right Symmetric Model (LRSM)~\cite{Pati:1974yy,Mohapatra:1974gc,Senjanovic:1975rk} 
170: is an economic and well-defined solution to a number discrepancies within the Standard Model of particle physics (SM).
171:  Such issues include: the origin and lightness of neutrino masses, the existence of dark matter, and 
172: the baryon-antibaryon asymmetry of the universe.
173: 
174: The model, based on the gauge group
175: \begin{equation}
176:  {\rm SU}(3)_c \otimes {\rm SU}(2)_L \otimes {\rm SU}(2)_R \otimes {\rm U}(1)_{B-L},
177: \end{equation}
178: predicts {right-handed (RH) currents and the existence of heavy, RH gauge bosons $W_R^\pm$ and $Z_R$. In addition,} the model contains 
179:  three RH neutrinos $N_R$ that are charged under ${\rm SU}(2)_R \otimes {\rm U}(1)_{B-L}$ but singlets under SM symmetries.
180: For masses up to several TeV, the LRSM can be tested at {collider experiments such as the Large Hadron Collider (LHC)}  through searches for processes like
181: \begin{eqnarray}
182:  p ~p \rightarrow	& \WR^\pm	& \rightarrow tb ~\text{or}~ N_R \ell^\pm, ~
183:  \quad\text{with}\quad N_R \rightarrow 	\ell^\pm W_R^{\mp *}  \rightarrow \ell^\pm q \overline{q'},
184:  \quad\text{and}
185:  \label{eq:ppWRff}
186:  \\
187:  p ~p \rightarrow	& \ZR		& \rightarrow t\overline{t} ~\text{or}~ N_R N_R,
188:  \quad\text{with}\quad \ell \in\{e,\mu,\tau\}, \quad q\in\{u,c,d,s,t,b\},
189:   \label{eq:ppZRff}
190: \end{eqnarray}
191: and are shown diagrammatically in Fig.~\ref{fig:production}.
192: The channels lead to {the distinct}  
193: $\ell^\pm\ell^\pm +nj$~\cite{Keung:1983uu}, $\ell^\pm+j$~\cite{Ferrari:2000sp,Mitra:2016kov}, and single top~\cite{Simmons:1996ws} topologies, 
194: and have been studied 
195: extensively~\cite{Han:2012vk,Chen:2013fna,Vasquez:2014mxa,Ng:2015hba,Dev:2015kca,Kang:2015uoc,FileviezPerez:2016erl,
196:   Frank:2010cj,Tello:2010am, Das:2012ii,  Maiezza:2015lza,Gluza:2015goa,Chakrabortty:2016wkl,Ferrari:2000sp,Mitra:2016kov,Simmons:1996ws}.

216: Monte Carlo (MC) modeling of the above processes by LHC experiments typically~\cite{Aad:2015xaa,Khachatryan:2014dka,ATLAS:2015nsi,Khachatryan:2015dcf}
217: involve leading order (LO) simulations matched to parton showers (PS)
218: and are normalized with constant factors, so-called $K$-factors, to account for QCD corrections.
219: 
220: While sufficient for predicting total inclusive cross sections,
221: the procedure does not correctly capture the kinematic changes 
222: induced  by high-transverse momentum $(p_T)$
223: initial-state radiation (ISR) or final-state radiation (FSR). 
224: This can substantially impact experimental sensitivity,
225: particularly as $\WR~(\ZR)$ decays to top quarks involve up to four (six) energetic jets at LO.
226: 
227: Jet matching schemes at a scale $\mu\ll M_{V_R}$, for $V_{R} = \WR,\ZR$,  can alleviate such problems.
228: However, missing virtual corrections give rise to potentially unstable soft/collinear logarithms of the 
229: form $\alpha_s(\MVR^2)\log(\MVR^2/\mu^{2})$ that spoil perturbative convergence for sufficiently large $(\MVR/\mu)$ ratios.
230: 
231: Furthermore, decays of high-mass RH gauge bosons to top quarks and heavy neutrinos can give rise to 
232: top~\cite{Baur:2007ck,Thaler:2008ju,Kaplan:2008ie} and heavy neutrino~\cite{Mitra:2016kov} jets, 
233: which carry different color charges, and hence possess different QCD radiation patterns.
234: Observables sensitive to the structure of these jets, e.g., jet mass, can be used to discriminate against SM backgrounds 
235: but require information that first arises with $\mathcal{O}(\as)$ corrections.
236: 
237: 
238: To resolve these complications, 
239: we present the automation of next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD corrections with parton shower (PS) matching for an 
240: effective LRSM, using the FeynRules (FR) + NLOCT + MadGraph5\_aMC@NLO (\mgamc)~\cite{Alloul:2013bka,Christensen:2008py,Degrande:2014vpa,Alwall:2014hca} 
241: framework.

243: The universal FR object (UFO) files~\cite{Degrande:2011ua} are publicly available from~\cite{nloFRModel} and require remarkably fewer 
244: inputs for simulating fully differential, benchmark collider processes 
245: than current LO implementations~\cite{Sjostrand:2006za,Ashry:2013loa,Roitgrund:2014zka}.

248: and a future 100 TeV Very Large Hadron Collider (VLHC)~\cite{Arkani-Hamed:2015vfh}.
249: We also present predictions for inclusive $N$ production at a hypothetical Large Hadron Electron Collider (LHeC)~\cite{AbelleiraFernandez:2012cc}.
250: The Born diagrams for these processes are shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:dydisProd}.
251: 
252: As a case study, we investigate at NLO+PS accuracy the properties of 
253: heavy neutrino (color-singlet) jets and top quark (color-triplet) jets from decays of high-mass $\WR$ bosons at the LHC.

274: \section{Effective Left-Right Symmetric Model}\label{sec:theory}
275: The Effective LRSM field content consists of the usual SM states, the $\WR^\pm$ and $\ZR$ gauge bosons, 
276: which are aligned with their mass eigenstates, and three heavy Majorana neutrinos $N_i$, 
277: aligned with the RH chiral states.
278: 
279: In the LRSM, the $\WR$ chiral coupling to quarks are given by
280: \begin{eqnarray}
281:  \mathcal{L}_{\WR-q-q'} = \frac{-\kappa_R^q g}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{i,j=u,d,\dots}\overline{u}_i V_{ij}^{\rm CKM'}~W_{R \mu}^+ \gamma^\mu P_R~ d_j + \text{H.c.},
282:  \label{chcurrent}
283: \end{eqnarray}
284: Here, $u_i (d_j)$ is an up-(down-)type quark of flavor $i (j)$; 
285: $P_{R(L)} = \frac{1}{2}(1\pm\gamma^5)$ denotes the RH(LH) chiral projection operator; and
286: $V_{ij}^{\rm CKM'}$  is the RH Cabbibo-Kobayashi-Masakawa (CKM) matrix, which is related to the SM CKM matrix.
287: Throughout this study, we will assume five massless quarks and take both the SM and RH CKM matrices to be diagonal with unit entries.
288: $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha_{\rm EM}(M_Z)}/\sin\theta_W$ is the SM Weak coupling constant and 
289: $\kappa_{R}^{q}\in\mathds{R}$ is an overall normalization for the $\WR$ interaction strength.
290: 
291: For leptons, the $\WR$ coupling and leptonic mixing is parametrized by~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Han:2012vk}
292: \begin{eqnarray}
293:  \mathcal{L}_{\WR-\ell-\nu/N} = \frac{-\kappa_R^\ell g}{\sqrt{2}}
294:  \sum_{\ell=e,\mu,\tau}
295:  \left[
296:  \sum_{m=1}^3	\overline{\nu^{c}_m} X_{\ell m} ~+~
297:  \sum_{m'=1}^3	\overline{N_{m'}} Y_{\ell m'}
298:  \right] ~W_{R \mu}^+ \gamma^\mu P_R~ \ell^-+\text{H.c.}
299: \end{eqnarray}
300: The matrix $Y_{\ell m'} (X_{\ell m})$ quantifies the mixing between 
301: the heavy (light) neutrino mass eigenstate $N_{m'}~(\nu_{m})$
302: and the RH chiral state with corresponding lepton flavor $\ell$. 
303: 
304: The mixing scale as~\cite{Keung:1983uu}
305: \begin{equation}
306: \vert Y_{\ell m'}\vert^2 \sim \mathcal{O}(1) \quad\text{and}\quad  
307: \vert X_{\ell m}\vert^2 \sim 1 - \vert Y_{\ell m'}\vert^2 \sim \mathcal{O}(m_{\nu_m}/m_{N_{m'}}).
308: \end{equation}
309: As in the quark sector, $\kappa_R^\ell\in\mathds{R}$ independently normalizes the $\WR$ coupling strength to leptons.
310: 
311: At TeV collider scales, both light neutrino masses and light neutrino mixing can be taken to zero.
312: So for simplicity, we take $Y_{\ell m'}$ to  be diagonal with unit entires:
313: \begin{equation}
314:   \vert Y_{e N}\vert = \vert Y_{\mu N_2}\vert = \vert Y_{\tau N_3}\vert = 1, \quad \vert Y_{\rm others}\vert = \vert X_{\ell m}\vert = 0.
315:   \label{eq:lrsmNuMixing}
316: \end{equation}
317: 
318: Mass and mixing assumptions are modifiable in the public model files~\cite{nloFRModel} but requires UFO regeneration.
319: Specifically, do not load the FR restrictions, ``massless.rst'' and ``diagonalCKM.rst''.
